alerts.title: AKI on TDF during gastroenteritis with dehydration: review TDF
alerts.message: Guidelines state that in patients on TDF admitted to hospital, creatinine (eGFR) must be checked even if monitoring criteria are not met, because intercurrent illness with dehydration or sepsis may cause renal deterioration. Creatinine rose from 0.9 mg/dL (2025-02-14) to 2.4 mg/dL today, with urea 58 mg/dL (urea:creatinine 24:1), hypotension, tachycardia, and dry mucosa, consistent with prerenal AKI from volume depletion. Competing explanations include TDF nephrotoxicity and DTG-related creatinine rise; however, DTG causes a creatinine rise under 30 umol/L (about 0.3 mg/dL), far below this change, and the picture favours prerenal AKI. Guidelines advise switching to ABC + 3TC + DTG if renal impairment develops due to TDF, with ABC/TAF alternatives for renal impairment.

evidence.recommended_action: Correct volume status and recheck creatinine/eGFR after rehydration. If renal impairment persists or is attributed to TDF, switch TDF to ABC (or TAF if eGFR 30-50 mL/min/1.73m2) with 3TC and DTG, per guideline.

alerts.title: Hypokalaemia and hyponatraemia: monitoring gap in acute illness
alerts.message: Potassium is 3.1 mmol/L and sodium 132 mmol/L with ongoing vomiting and diarrhoea, in a patient on TDF whose renal function is acutely impaired. The guideline excerpts provided do not specify electrolyte thresholds or management, so this cannot be fully attributed to a guideline rule; it is an evident gap in the plan, which does not mention electrolyte replacement or repeat electrolytes.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat electrolytes and renal function after fluid resuscitation, and replace potassium and sodium as clinically indicated. Confirm this against local protocols, as the provided excerpts do not specify.
